page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. The configuration features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing 2.0 threads per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top tier, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as the stress-ng multi-core CPU test and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, perform in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark CPU and memory scores, also align with the average tier. For language model workloads, the server demonstrates strong performance in text generation using a small 135M model, but drops to the weak tier for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8as_v7 offers a standard resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of local NVMe storage. The high single-core performance makes it efficient for tasks sensitive to single-threaded execution speeds, such as certain database operations, web serving, and lightweight text processing. However, the lack of local storage requires external disk attachment, which should be factored into the overall architectural design. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, Redis caching, and general-purpose application hosting.
